rationale: The carrier's new ingredient (dltr) is mechanically near-collinear with the weight's gross issuance (dltis) — firms that retire debt are almost definitionally the ones that issue it — so the product largely ranks gross debt turnover/size rather than the hypothesized refinancing shortfall, making it an ambiguous extension of the archive's DebtFinancedPayoutShortfall rather than a clean test of it.

The proposal itself concedes the carrier is essentially NEG(oancf/at) and the weight is identical to AccrualOpacityFinancingDependence's, so this is a low-cash-profitability × net-external-financing composite that recombines two well-known published anomalies with no new economic content beyond a decomposition diagnostic.

Internally inconsistent — dividing the deficit by the debt stock makes the signal *smaller* for heavily indebted firms and explosively large for near-zero-debt firms, the exact opposite of the stated "a given shortfall is more threatening with a large existing debt load," and it also discards the cross-theme interaction to become a single winsorized ratio dominated by denominator noise.

The MIN(dvt, sstk) conjunction is a genuinely untested and economically interpretable "pay-and-raise" state whose sign direction is consistent with the accrual carrier, though it risks proxying for industry composition (utilities, REITs, financials) and thin coverage among simultaneous payers/issuers.

The escalation-of-commitments mechanism is distinct from the archive's level-of-deficit winner and the sign logic is coherent, but because Δdvt/at is an order of magnitude smaller than Δdebt/at the MIN weight will almost always reduce to the dividend change, so it is effectively "deficit × dividend increase" rather than the advertised joint escalation.

Since the RANK weight is strictly non-negative, this is the known net-external-financing anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) amplified by the accruals anomaly using the same variable pair as the archive's AccrualOpacityFinancingDependence with only the winsor/rank transforms swapped — a transform-level rather than economic restructuring.
